title: Property-(P) DG modules are homotopically projective
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$; its cohomology is $H^i(M)=\ker(d:M^i\to M^{i+1})/d(M^{i-1})$, and a quasi-isomorphism is a homomorphism of differential graded modules (degree-preserving, $A$-linear, commuting with the differentials) inducing isomorphisms on all $H^i$. For $k\in\mathbf Z$ let $A[k]$ be the shifted module with $A[k]^i=A^{i+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_A$ and right action by multiplication. Say that a right differential graded $A$-module $P$ has property (P) if there is a filtration $0=F_0P\subset F_1P\subset F_2P\subset\cdots$ by differential graded submodules such that $P=\bigcup_{n\geq0}F_nP$, each inclusion $F_nP\subset F_{n+1}P$ admits a left inverse as a map of graded right $A$-modules (not necessarily commuting with $d$), and each quotient $F_{n+1}P/F_nP$ is isomorphic, as a differential graded $A$-module, to a direct sum $\bigoplus_{j\in J_n}A[k_{nj}]$ over a set $J_n$ (possibly empty) with integers $k_{nj}$. Let $P$ be a right differential graded $A$-module with property (P). For any right differential graded $A$-module $N$, let $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(P,N)^r$ consist of degree-$r$ additive graded right $A$-linear maps $f$, with $f(pa)=f(p)a$ and differential $\delta f=d_Nf-(-1)^rfd_P$. If $N$ is acyclic, meaning $H^i(N)=0$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, this Hom complex is acyclic. Equivalently, every chain map $P\to N$ to an acyclic right differential graded module is null-homotopic, and the same holds with $N$ replaced by any integer shift. Thus $P$ is homotopically projective. No boundedness, commutativity or countability hypothesis on $A$, $P$, $N$ or the filtration quotient index sets is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $r\in\mathbf Z$ and a degree-$r$ cocycle $f$, so $d_Nf=(-1)^rfd_P$. We construct compatible degree-$(r-1)$ graded right $A$-linear maps $h_n:F_nP\to N$ satisfying $d_Nh_n+(-1)^rh_nd_P=f|_{F_nP}$. At $n=0$ take the zero map on $F_0P=0$. In the induction step suppose $h_n$ has been constructed. All subsequent choices concern only the next filtration stage, and the extension will agree with $h_n$ on $F_nP$.

proof.text: Write $Q_n=F_{n+1}P/F_nP$ and choose the given dg isomorphism $\bigoplus_{j\in J_n}A[k_{nj}]\cong Q_n$. Let $\rho_n:F_{n+1}P\to F_nP$ be a graded retraction and $i_n$ the inclusion. The formula $s_n([x])=x-i_n\rho_n(x)$ is independent of the lift $x$, since $\rho_ni_n=1$, and is a graded right-linear section of the quotient. Lift the unit of the $j$th summand to $e_j=s_n(1_j)$ of degree $q_j=-k_{nj}$. The identity $d_A1=d_A(1\cdot1)=2d_A1$ gives $d_A1=0$, so $d_Pe_j\in F_nP$. The section and the quotient isomorphism give a graded direct-sum decomposition $F_{n+1}P=F_nP\oplus\bigoplus_j e_jA$: each element has a unique expression $x+\sum_j e_ja_j$ with finitely many nonzero coefficients.

proof.text: For each $j$ set $z_j=f(e_j)-(-1)^rh_n(d_Pe_j)\in N^{q_j+r}$. The cocycle equation for $f$ gives $d_Nf(e_j)=(-1)^rf(d_Pe_j)$. The inductive equation, evaluated on $d_Pe_j\in F_nP$, gives $d_Nh_n(d_Pe_j)=f(d_Pe_j)$ because $d_P^2e_j=0$. Subtracting these two equations shows $d_Nz_j=0$.

source.place: Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, with the filtration of Tag 09KK, section-P-resolutions. Direct cell-by-cell null-homotopy extension written by NN; the generator calculation is the defining computation underlying Tag 09K1, lemma-hom-from-shift-free.

proof.text: Since $H^{q_j+r}(N)=0$, the definition $H=\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$ gives $y_j\in N^{q_j+r-1}$ with $d_Ny_j=z_j$. Choose one such primitive for each $j\in J_n$. Using the direct-sum decomposition from Step 2 define $h_{n+1}(x+\sum_j e_ja_j)=h_n(x)+\sum_j y_ja_j$. Every sum here is finite. Uniqueness of that decomposition makes this a well-defined additive graded right $A$-linear map of degree $r-1$, extending $h_n$.

proof.text:
The required equation already holds on $F_nP$. On a new generator times a homogeneous $a\in A$ the two module Leibniz rules give
$$\begin{aligned}(d_Nh_{n+1}+(-1)^rh_{n+1}d_P)(e_ja)&=(d_Ny_j+(-1)^rh_n(d_Pe_j))a\\&\quad+\big((-1)^{q_j+r-1}+(-1)^{q_j+r}\big)y_jd_Aa\\&=f(e_j)a=f(e_ja).\end{aligned}$$
Here $d_P(e_ja)=(d_Pe_j)a+(-1)^{q_j}e_jd_Aa$, so the displayed cancellation uses no commutation of elements of $A$. Additivity and the decomposition prove the equation on all of $F_{n+1}P$, completing the induction step.

proof.text: Recursion in $n$ therefore produces compatible $h_n$. For a homogeneous $p\in P$ choose $n$ with $p\in F_nP$ and put $h(p)=h_n(p)$. If two stages contain $p$, their values agree in the larger stage. A common stage for two elements, or for $p$ and $pa$, proves additivity and right linearity of $h$, and $h$ has degree $r-1$. Since each $F_nP$ is a dg submodule, $p$ and $d_Pp$ lie in the same stage, and its equation gives $d_Nh(p)+(-1)^rh(d_Pp)=f(p)$. Thus $\delta h=f$. This works for every integer $r$ and every cocycle $f$, proving acyclicity of the Hom complex.

source.place: Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective, with the filtration of Tag 09KK, section-P-resolutions. Direct cell-by-cell null-homotopy extension written by NN; the generator calculation is the defining computation underlying Tag 09K1, lemma-hom-from-shift-free.

proof.text: In degree zero $\delta h=d_Nh+hd_P$, so the construction gives a null-homotopy of every chain map $P\to N$. Every $N[t]$ remains acyclic: multiplying its differential by $(-1)^t$ changes neither kernel nor image, so $H^i(N[t])=H^{i+t}(N)=0$. The conclusion applies to all these shifts. Conversely a degree-$r$ Hom cocycle is a chain map $P\to N[r]$; if $s$ is a null-homotopy for that map, then $(-1)^rd_Ns+sd_P=f$. Setting $h=(-1)^rs$ gives $\delta h=f$, verifying the stated equivalence in every degree.
